authoredPrompt: This figure shows a spherical wedge in 3D, the volume element used for triple integration in spherical coordinates. The wedge is a small solid (shown with orange, yellow, and green faces) bounded by six surfaces: two spherical shells at radii rho1 and rho2 (marked along the z-axis), two vertical half-planes at azimuthal angles theta1 and theta2 (shown in the horizontal plane near the base), and two cones at polar angles phi1 and phi2 (measured from the z-axis and indicated by arcs). The bounding surfaces are rendered transparently to reveal the wedge's position inside the overall spherical sector. The figure defines the spherical wedge as the three-dimensional analogue of the polar rectangle and identifies its six bounding surfaces in terms of the spherical coordinates rho, theta, and phi.
authoredInteractions:
- Sliders for ρ₁ and ρ₂: expand or contract the radial bounds of the wedge and watch the volume element resize within the spherical shell
- Sliders for θ₁/θ₂ and φ₁/φ₂: sweep the azimuthal and polar angle bounds and observe the colored wedge element rotate and tilt through the shell
- Drag to rotate the 3D view to inspect the spherical coordinate wedge from any direction
authoredContext:
By a spherical wedge or spherical element
of volume we mean a solid enclosed between six surfaces of the following form:
two spheres (green) ρ = ρ1,ρ = ρ2 (ρ1 <ρ2)
two vertical half-planes (yellow) θ = θ1,θ = θ2 (θ1 <θ2)
nappes of two circular cones (pink) φ = φ1,φ = φ2 (φ1 <φ2)
(Figure 14.6.7). We will refer to the numbers ρ2 − ρ1,θ2 − θ1, and φ2 − φ1 as the dimensions of a spherical wedge.
sourceQmd: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 14.6.7

discrepancies: The ρ₁/ρ₂ dimension arrows sit immediately beside the z-axis and their labels float over/near the wedge, whereas the source places them clearly to the left with long extension lines

The wedge in the source shows distinctly colored faces (green outer, orange side, khaki front) in a balanced arrangement; in the render the green outer face dominates and the yellow inner face and khaki/olive plane faces are barely visible
The φ arcs in the source are drawn with arrowheads indicating the angular sweep from the z-axis; the generated arcs are plain lines without arrowheads
The translucent shell in the source reads as a quarter-sphere sector with visible flat cut faces; the generated shell is a smooth ghosted dome without the planar cutaway look
evaluation.notes: A faithful, well-interactive spherical wedge figure with correct axes, arcs, and six working bound sliders; main weaknesses are the cramped ρ dimension arrows/labels and the dominance of the green face hiding the other colored faces.
action_items: Move the ρ₁/ρ₂ dimension arrows further left of the z-axis with proper extension lines so they and their labels do not overlap the wedge
Adjust the default wedge bounds or camera so the orange cone faces and khaki half-plane faces are visible alongside the green outer face, matching the source's multi-face coloring
Add small arrowheads to the θ and φ arcs to match the source's swept-angle notation
